verdict.rationale: dlt's docs say it infers schemas and data types, normalizes and unnests nested data into well-structured datasets, and deduplicates or upserts by primary_key under the merge disposition. The loaded tables can then be queried via pipeline.dataset() with SQL, Ibis or dataframes, and a community user praises the schema auto-generation and flattening for producing cleaner tables. missing for 10: detailed docs on destination type mapping and column typing, evidence that deduplication works by default rather than only when merge is configured with a primary_key, hands-on corroboration of deduplicated typed tables.

support.subject: As an analytics engineer, loaded data lands as typed, deduplicated destination tables ready to query, not raw JSON blobs

citations.quote: dlt infers schemas and data types, normalizes the data, and handles nested data structures.
dlt will take care of the rest: unnesting the data, inferring the schema, etc., and writing to the destination.
Merge: Merges new data into the destination using merge_key and/or deduplicates/upserts new data using primary_key.
dlt is an open-source Python library that loads data from various, often messy data sources into well-structured datasets.
use `pipeline.dataset()` to query the data. You can build the query with data frame expressions, Ibis, or SQL.
especially the schema auto-generation and flattening will make many raw data tables look much cleaner.
